english.heading: Food Forest Design
body: Build a living food system in layers.
Grow food from tall canopy down to root crops.
Use vertical space, soil life, shade, and moisture together.
Learn how to design and establish a food forest for your farm.

heading.text: Ku Hlela Food Forest
heading.backTranslation: To Plan a Food Forest

body.text: Aka sisiteme ya swakudya leyi hanyaka hi swiyenge swo hambana.
body.backTranslation: Build a food system that lives in different layers.

body.text: Byala swakudya ku suka eka canopy ya mirhi yo leha ku fika eka root crops.
body.backTranslation: Plant food from the canopy of tall trees down to root crops.

body.text: Tirhisa ndhawu ya le henhla ni le hansi, leswi hanyaka emisaveni, ndzhuti ni ku tsakama swin’we.
body.backTranslation: Use the space above and below, what lives in the soil, shade and moisture together.

body.text: Dyondza ku hlela ni ku sungula food forest epurasini ra wena.
body.backTranslation: Learn to plan and start a food forest on your farm.

english.heading: Why This Matters
body: A food forest grows useful plants at different heights.
Good design can combine harvests, shade and soil cover. Plants still compete for light, water and nutrients.
Plan the care you can provide and watch how the planting changes.

heading.text: Ha yini leswi swi ri swa nkoka
heading.backTranslation: Why this is important

body.text: Food forest yi kurisa swimilana leswi pfunaka leswi nga ni ku leha ko hambana.
body.backTranslation: Food forest grows plants that help that have different heights.

body.text: Nkunguhato lowunene wu nga hlanganisa ntshovelo, ndzhuti ni ku funengeta misava. Swimilana swa ha phikizana hi ku vonakala, mati ni nutrients.
body.backTranslation: A good plan can combine harvest, shade and covering the soil. Plants still compete for light, water and nutrients.

body.text: Hlela nhlayiso lowu u nga kotaka ku wu endla, kutani u languta ndlela leyi swimilana swi cincaka ha yona.
body.backTranslation: Plan maintenance that you can manage to do, then watch how the plants change.

english.heading: Learning Outcomes
body: Name the seven commonly described food-forest layers.
Check plants against your site, local ecology and the approved project list.
Plan establishment and ongoing care without assuming a fixed date for harvest or canopy closure.

heading.text: Leswi u nga ta kota ku swi endla
heading.backTranslation: What you will be able to do

body.text: Boxa swiyenge swa 7 leswi tolovelekeke ku hlamusela food forest.
body.backTranslation: Box the 7 layers that are commonly used to describe a food forest.

body.text: Kambela swimilana hi ku ya hi ndhawu ya wena, ecology ya laha kaya, ni approved project list.
body.backTranslation: Check plants according to your place, the local ecology, and the approved project list.

body.text: Hlela ku sungula ka swimilana ni nhlayiso lowu yaka emahlweni, u nga teki leswaku ku ta va ni siku leri tiyeke ra ntshovelo kumbe ra ku pfaleka ka canopy.
body.backTranslation: Plan the start of the plants and the care that goes ahead, do not assume that there will be a firm day of harvest or of canopy closing.

english.heading: The Forest Uses Every Layer
body: An indigenous forest fills the space from the highest branches to the roots.
Different plants use the light and moisture available at their level.
A food forest copies this pattern with productive species.
The result is not one crop in one row, but many useful layers growing together.

heading.text: Nhova yi tirhisa swiyenge hinkwato
heading.backTranslation: The forest uses all the layers

body.text: Indigenous forest yi tata ndhawu ku sukela eka marhavi ya yona ya le henhla swinene ku fika eka timitsu.
body.backTranslation: An indigenous forest fills the space from its very highest branches down to the roots.

body.text: Swimilana swo hambana swi tirhisa ku vonakala na ku tsakama loku kumekaka eka xiyenge xa swona.
body.backTranslation: Different plants use the light and the moisture found in their layer.

body.text: Food forest yi landzela xivumbeko lexi hi ku tirhisa tinxaka ta swimilana leswi humesaka vuyelo.
body.backTranslation: Food forest follows a pattern/form by using kinds of plants that produce results (yield).

body.text: Vuyelo a hi xibyariwa xin’we eka layini yin’we, kambe i swiyenge swo tala leswi pfunaka swi ri karhi swi kula swin’we.
body.backTranslation: The yield is not one crop on one line, but many layers that help while they grow together.

english.heading: Watch: Read the Seven Planting Layers
body: Find seven planting layers.
Tall trees form the canopy.
Smaller trees grow below it.
Then look for woody shrubs.
Herbaceous plants have soft stems.
Ground cover spreads across the surface.
Root crops grow below the surface.
Climbers use suitable supports.
These are planning layers, not fixed height bands. Choose plants and spacing for your site.

heading.text: Languta: Hlaya Swiyenge swa 7 swa Ku Byala
heading.backTranslation: Look: Read the 7 Layers of Planting

body.text: Kuma swiyenge swa 7 swa ku byala.
body.backTranslation: Find the 7 layers of planting.

body.text: Mirhi yo leha yi vumba canopy.
body.backTranslation: Tall trees form the canopy.

body.text: Mirhi leyitsongo yi kula ehansi ka canopy.
body.backTranslation: Small trees grow below the canopy.

body.text: Kutani languta swihlahla swa murhi.
body.backTranslation: Come and look after the medicinal [?] trees/shrubs. ("Kutani" = come (plural/imperative); "languta" = look after/look at; "swihlahla" = trees/shrubs; "swa murhi" = of medicine/of a tree [?] — "murhi" can mean medicine or tree, so "medicinal shrubs" or "shrubs of trees" [?]).

body.text: Swimilana swa herbaceous swi ni swiphunga swo olova.
body.backTranslation: Herbaceous plants have soft stems [?].

body.text: Swimilana leswi funengetaka misava swi hangalaka ehenhla ka misava.
body.backTranslation: Plants that cover the soil spread above the ground.

body.text: Root crops swi kula ehansi ka misava.
body.backTranslation: Root crops grow under the soil.

body.text: Swimilana swo khandziya swi tirhisa switiyiso leswi faneleke.
body.backTranslation: Climbing plants use suitable supports.

body.text: Leswi i swiyenge swo hlela, a hi swiyenge swa ku leha leswi nga cinciki. Hlawula swimilana ni ndhawu leyi nga exikarhi ka swona hi ku ya hi ndhawu ya wena.
body.backTranslation: These are layers for planning, they are not layers of unchanging heights. Choose plants and the space that is between them according to your place.

english.heading: The Seven Layers
body: Think of tall canopy, smaller trees, shrubs and herbaceous plants.
Ground cover protects the surface, root crops grow below it, and climbers use suitable supports.
The heights and spacing depend on the plants and site. These are planning layers, not fixed height bands.

heading.text: Swiyenge swa 7
heading.backTranslation: 7 layers

body.text: Anakanyisa hi canopy yo leha, mirhi leyitsongo, swihlahla ni swimilana swa herbaceous.
body.backTranslation: Think about the tall canopy, small trees, shrubs and herbaceous plants.

body.text: Swimilana leswi funengetaka misava swi sirhelela ehenhla ka misava, root crops swi kula ehansi ka yona, naswona swimilana swo khandziya swi tirhisa switiyiso leswi faneleke.
body.backTranslation: Plants that cover the soil protect above the ground, root crops grow below it, and climbing plants use suitable supports.

body.text: Ku leha ni ndhawu leyi nga exikarhi ka swimilana swi titshege hi swimilana ni ndhawu. Leswi i swiyenge swo hlela, a hi swiyenge swa ku leha leswi nga cinciki.
body.backTranslation: Height and the space that is between plants depend on the plants and the place. These are layers for planning, they are not layers of unchanging heights.

english.heading: Read a Layered Planting Example
body: The original Highveld example includes Wild Fig or pecan above lemon, naartjie and black mulberry.
It places Cape gooseberry and Wild Medlar with vegetables, wild garlic, sweet potato and granadilla.
Treat this as a layout example, not permission to plant every species. Check identity, frost tolerance, mature size and local restrictions first.

heading.text: Hlaya Xikombiso xa Ku Byala hi Swiyenge
heading.backTranslation: Read the Example of Planting by Layers

body.text: Xikombiso xo sungula xa le Highveld xi katsa Wild Fig kumbe pecan ehenhla ka lemon, naartjie ni black mulberry.
body.backTranslation: A starting example for the Highveld includes Wild Fig or pecan above lemon, naartjie and black mulberry.

body.text: Xi veka Cape gooseberry ni Wild Medlar swin’we ni miroho, wild garlic, sweet potato ni granadilla.
body.backTranslation: It places Cape gooseberry and Wild Medlar together with vegetables, wild garlic, sweet potato and granadilla.

body.text: Teka leswi tanihi xikombiso xa ku vekiwa ka swimilana, a hi mpfumelelo wo byala tinxaka hinkwato. Rhanga u kambela leswi swi nga xiswona, frost tolerance, vukulu bya swona loko swi kurile ni swiyimiso swa laha kaya.
body.backTranslation: Take this as an example of the placing of plants, it is not permission to plant all kinds. First check what they are, frost tolerance, their size when they have grown and the local regulations/standards.

english.heading: Care Changes as Plants Grow
body: Young plants need establishment care: moisture checks, weed control and protection from damage.
As plants grow, shade and leaf litter change conditions below them.
Check competition and access. Prune, thin or adjust lower planting when observations call for it; the system does not become care-free on a fixed birthday.

heading.text: Nhlayiso yi cinca loko swimilana swi kula
heading.backTranslation: Maintenance changes when the plants grow

body.text: Swimilana leswitsongo swi lava nhlayiso wa ku sungula: ku kambela mati ya le misaveni, ku lawula swimilana leswi nga lavekiki ni ku sirheleriwa eka ku onhaka.
body.backTranslation: Small plants need starting care: checking the water in the soil, controlling plants that are not wanted, and being protected from damage/spoiling [?].

body.text: Loko swimilana swi ri karhi swi kula, ndzhuti na leaf litter swi cinca xiyimo xa le hansi ka swona.
body.backTranslation: While plants are growing, shade and leaf litter change the condition of the ground beneath them.

body.text: Kambela ku phikizana ni ndlela yo fikelela. Tsema marhavi, susa swimilana leswi hlawuriweke hi ku helela kumbe lulamisa ku byala ka le hansi loko leswi u swi voneke swi vula tano; sisiteme a yi hundzuki yo nga lavi nhlayiso hi siku leri tiyeke.
body.backTranslation: Check competition and the way of access. Cut branches, remove chosen plants completely, or adjust the lower planting when what you have seen says so; the system does not become one that needs no maintenance on a firm day.

english.heading: Choose for Your Site
body: Check local rainfall, frost, heat, soil and water availability before choosing plants.
Mango can suffer frost damage. Quince needs suitable winter chilling for reliable cropping.
A regional label or a sheltered corner is not enough. Confirm each plant and variety with reliable local guidance.

heading.text: Hlawula hi ku ya hi Ndhawu ya Wena
heading.backTranslation: Choose according to Your Place

body.text: Kambela mpfula ya laha, xiqhwa, ku hisa, misava ni mati lama kumekaka u nga si hlawula swimilana.
body.backTranslation: Check the local rain, frost, heat, soil and available water before you choose plants.

body.text: Mango yi nga onhiwa hi xiqhwa. Quince yi lava winter chilling leyi faneleke leswaku yi humesa mihandzu hi ndlela leyi tshembekaka.
body.backTranslation: Mango can be damaged by frost. Quince needs suitable winter chilling so that it produces fruit reliably.

body.text: Vito ra xifundzha kumbe ndhawu yin'we leyi sirhelelekeke a swi ringananga. Tiyisisa swimilana swin'wana ni swin'wana ni tinxaka ta swona hi ndzayo leyi tshembekaka ya laha kaya.
body.backTranslation: The name of a province/district [?] or one protected place is not enough. Make sure of each and every plant and their kinds with advice that is trustworthy from where home is / local [?].

english.heading: Watch: Match the Species to the Climate
body: Climate decides which species belong.
On the Highveld, choose cold-tolerant trees and shrubs; on the KZN coast and Lowveld, choose warm-climate species.
Match every plant to your site.

heading.text: Languta: Fambisa Tinxaka ni Xiyimo xa Moya
heading.backTranslation: Look: Match Kinds and Climate

body.text: Xiyimo xa moya xi hlawula leswaku i tinxaka tihi leti fanelaka.
body.backTranslation: The condition of the air/weather determines which kinds are suitable.

body.text: Eka Highveld, hlawula mirhi ni swihlahla leswi tiyiselaka vuhola; eka KZN coast ni Lowveld, hlawula tinxaka ta ndhawu leyi hisaka.
body.backTranslation: On the Highveld, choose trees and shrubs that tolerate cold; on the KZN coast and Lowveld, choose kinds of a hot area.

body.text: Fambisa swimilana hinkwaswo ni ndhawu ya wena.
body.backTranslation: Match all the plants with your place.

english.heading: Check the Highveld Examples
body: The original list includes pecan, walnut and indigenous fig; apple, pear, plum, black mulberry and loquat; rosemary, Wild Medlar, Cape gooseberry and Barbados cherry.
This list is not a blanket recommendation. Check each plant against frost, soil, mature size and the approved local species list.
Keep existing legal and project restrictions in force. Do not plant from a picture alone.

heading.text: Kambela Swikombiso swa Highveld
heading.backTranslation: Check Highveld Examples

body.text: Lisiti yo sungula yi katsa pecan, walnut ni indigenous fig; apple, pear, plum, black mulberry ni loquat; rosemary, Wild Medlar, Cape gooseberry ni Barbados cherry.
body.backTranslation: A starting list includes pecan, walnut and indigenous fig; apple, pear, plum, black mulberry and loquat; rosemary, Wild Medlar, Cape gooseberry and Barbados cherry.

body.text: Lisiti leyi a hi xitsundzuxo lexi tirhaka eka swimilana hinkwaswo ni swiyimo hinkwaswo. Kambela swimilana swin’wana ni swin’wana hi xiqhwa, misava, vukulu bya swona loko swi kurile ni approved local species list.
body.backTranslation: This list is not a recommendation that works for all plants and all conditions. Check each plant by cold/frost, soil, their size when they have grown and approved local species list.

body.text: Swiyimiso swa nawu ni swa phurojeke leswi nga kona swi fanele ku tshama swi tirha. U nga byali hi ku vona xifaniso ntsena.
body.backTranslation: The existing legal and project rules must always keep working. Do not plant by seeing a picture only.

english.heading: Check the Warm-Region Examples
body: The original warm-region examples include mango, avocado, Natal Mahogany, banana, pawpaw, litchi, Wild Fig, Barbados cherry and Wild Dagga.
Marula, Mopane and baobab also appear in the Limpopo examples. Local suitability still needs checking.
Useful trees are not automatically edible. Confirm identity and safe use; a landscape photograph is not a food-identification guide.

heading.text: Kambela Swikombiso swa Ndhawu leyi Hisaka
heading.backTranslation: Check Examples of a Hot Area

body.text: Swikombiso swo sungula swa ndhawu leyi hisaka swi katsa mango, avocado, Natal Mahogany, banana, pawpaw, litchi, Wild Fig, Barbados cherry ni Wild Dagga.
body.backTranslation: Starting examples for a hot place/area include mango, avocado, Natal Mahogany, banana, pawpaw, litchi, Wild Fig, Barbados cherry and Wild Dagga.

body.text: Marula, Mopane ni baobab swi tlhela swi humelela eka swikombiso swa Limpopo. Ku fanela ka laha kaya ku ha lava ku kambeliwa.
body.backTranslation: Marula, Mopane and baobab also appear in the Limpopo examples. Local suitability still needs to be checked.

body.text: Ku va mirhi yi pfuna a swi vuli leswaku yi nga dyiwa. Tiyisisa leswi yi nga xiswona ni ku yi tirhisa hi ndlela leyi sirhelelekeke; xifaniso xa ndhawu a hi nkongomiso wo tiva leswaku i swakudya swihi.
body.backTranslation: That trees help does not say that they can be eaten. Make sure what they are and use them in a safe way; a picture of a place is not a guide to know which are foods.

english.heading: Include Locally Appropriate Indigenous Plants
body: Locally appropriate indigenous plants can support habitat as part of the design.
Choose for your ecosystem and the useful role of each plant. There is no sourced percentage target in this lesson.
Protect existing natural vegetation. Do not turn healthy grassland into a food forest simply because trees are useful elsewhere.

heading.text: Katsa swimilana indigenous leswi faneleke laha
heading.backTranslation: Include suitable indigenous plants here

body.text: Swimilana indigenous leswi faneleke laha kaya swi nga seketela habitat tanihi xiphemu xa nkunguhato.
body.backTranslation: Indigenous plants suitable to the local area can support habitat as part of the plan.

body.text: Hlawula hi ku ya hi ecosystem ya wena ni ntirho wa nkoka wa swimilana swin’wana ni swin’wana. A ku na xikongomelo xa phesenti lexi nga ni xihlovo eka dyondzo leyi.
body.backTranslation: Choose according to your ecosystem and the important role of each plant. There is no percentage target that has a source in this lesson.

body.text: Sirhelela swimilana swa ntumbuluko leswi nga kona. U nga hundzuli ndhawu ya byanyi leyi nga ni rihanyo yi va food forest ntsena hikuva mirhi yi pfuna kun’wana.
body.backTranslation: Protect the natural plants that are there. Do not turn a healthy grass area into a food forest only because trees help elsewhere.

english.heading: Plan the Sequence for the Site
body: Start by checking the site, water supply and care available. Protect exposed soil early.
Temporary support plants may provide shelter and useful cut material where appropriate.
Main trees and lower layers can be introduced as conditions allow. Ground cover need not wait until the end; avoid plants competing with young trees.

heading.text: Hlela Ku Landzelelana ka Ndhawu
heading.backTranslation: Plan the Sequence of the Place

body.text: Sungula hi ku kambela ndhawu, mati lama kumekaka ni nhlayiso lowu u nga wu endlaka. Sirhelela misava leyi nga funengetiwangiki eku sunguleni.
body.backTranslation: Begin by checking the place, the water that is available and the care that you can do. Protect soil that is not covered at the start.

body.text: Support plants swa nkarhi wo koma swi nga nyika xisirhelelo ni swilo leswi tsemiweke leswi pfunaka laha swi faneleke.
body.backTranslation: Support plants of a short time can give protection and cut material that helps where suitable.

body.text: Mirhi leyikulu ni swiyenge swa le hansi swi nga engeteriwa loko swiyimo swi pfumelela. Swimilana leswi funengetaka misava a swi lavi ku rindza ku fika emakumu; papalata swimilana leswi phikizanaka ni mirhi leyintshwa.
body.backTranslation: Big trees and the lower layers can be added if conditions allow. Plants that cover the ground do not need to wait until the end; avoid plants that compete with new trees.

english.heading: Watch: Care for a Young Food Forest
body: This picture shows a young food forest. Start with an area you can care for.
Protect exposed soil early. Here, loose mulch covers the soil.
Keep mulch away from the trunk. Notice the clear space at the tree's base.
Watch for competition. The farmer is removing grass near the young tree.
Before adding more plants, check moisture, shelter and the care you can provide. Let what you observe guide your next step.

heading.text: Languta: Hlayisa Food Forest leyitsongo
heading.backTranslation: Look: Maintain a small Food Forest

body.text: Xifaniso lexi xi komba food forest leyitsongo. Sungula hi ndhawu leyi u nga yi hlayisaka.
body.backTranslation: This picture shows a small food forest. Start with a place that you can maintain.

body.text: Sirhelela misava leyi nga funengetiwangiki eku sunguleni. Laha, mulch wo olova wu funengeta misava.
body.backTranslation: Protect soil that is not covered at the start. Here, light mulch covers the soil.

body.text: Hlayisa mulch kule ni nsinya wa murhi. Xiya ndhawu leyi pfulekeke ehansi swinene ka nsinya wa murhi.
body.backTranslation: Keep mulch far from the trunk of the tree. Notice the open space very low/near the bottom at the trunk of the tree.

body.text: Tivonele ku phikizana. Mulimi u susa byanyi ekusuhi ni murhi lowutsongo.
body.backTranslation: Watch for competition. The farmer removes grass/weeds near the small tree.

body.text: U nga si engetela swimilana swin’wana, kambela ku tsakama, xisirhelelo ni nhlayiso lowu u nga wu endlaka. Tshika leswi u swi xiyaka swi kongomisa goza leri landzelaka.
body.backTranslation: Before adding other plants, check moisture, protection and the maintenance you can do. Leave what you notice to direct the next step.

english.heading: Prepare a Manageable First Area
body: Begin with an area you can water and maintain. Check existing vegetation before clearing.
Where appropriate, plain cardboard under suitable mulch can suppress unwanted growth. Keep water able to enter the soil and leave trunks clear.
Plan spacing from mature plant size. Prepare nursery plants for the next suitable planting opportunity.

heading.text: Lulamisa Ndhawu yo Sungula leyi Hlayisekaka
heading.backTranslation: Prepare a Starting Place that can be Maintained

body.text: Sungula hi ndhawu leyi u nga yi cheletaka mati ni ku yi hlayisa. Kambela swimilana leswi nga kona u nga si yi basisa.
body.backTranslation: Start with a place that you can water and maintain. Check the plants that are there before you clear it.

body.text: Laha swi faneleke, cardboard ya ntolovelo ehansi ka mulch lowu faneleke yi nga sivela ku mila loku nga lavekiki. Tshika mati ma kota ku nghena emisaveni, u tshika swinsinya swi basile.
body.backTranslation: Where suitable, ordinary cardboard under suitable mulch can prevent unwanted growth. Let water be able to enter the soil, and leave the trunks clean.

body.text: Hlela ndhawu leyi nga exikarhi ka swimilana hi ku ya hi vukulu bya swona loko swi kurile. Lunghiselela nursery plants nkarhi wo byala lowu landzelaka lowu faneleke.
body.backTranslation: Plan the space that is in between plants according to their size when they have grown. Prepare nursery plants for the next suitable planting time.

english.heading: Adjust as the Trees Grow
body: Watch how shade, roots and available water affect neighbouring plants.
Comfrey and wild garlic appear in the original underplanting example; check their local suitability before use.
Prune or thin support plants when needed, using methods suited to each species. Suitable clean cuttings can return as mulch. Do not wait for a fixed year if competition is already harming plants.

heading.text: Lulamisa Loko Mirhi Yi Kula
heading.backTranslation: Adjust When Trees Grow

body.text: Languta ndlela leyi ndzhuti, timitsu ni mati lama kumekaka swi khumbaka ha yona swimilana leswi nga ekusuhi.
body.backTranslation: Watch how shade, roots and available water affect the plants that are near.

body.text: Comfrey ni wild garlic swi kumeka eka xikombiso xo sungula xa swimilana leswi byariweke ehansi ka mirhi; kambela ku fanela ka swona laha kaya u nga si swi tirhisa.
body.backTranslation: Comfrey and wild garlic are found in a starting example of plants/herbs that are planted underneath trees; check their suitability at home [?] ("laha kaya" = where home is / locally) before you use them.

body.text: Tsema marhavi ya support plants kumbe u susa support plants hi ku helela loko swi laveka, u tirhisa tindlela leti fanelaka xinxaka xin’wana ni xin’wana. Switsemiwa leswi faneleke leswi basileke swi nga tlhela swi va mulch. U nga rindzi lembe leri tiyeke loko ku phikizana se ku onha swimilana.
body.backTranslation: Cut the branches of support plants or remove support plants completely when needed, using methods that suit each kind. Suitable cuttings that are clean can also become mulch. Do not wait for a firm year when competition is already damaging the plants.

english.heading: Plant with Reliable Moisture
body: Choose a planting opportunity when soil moisture and expected weather support establishment.
Rain can help, but check the root zone and keep a backup watering plan. Avoid planting into waterlogged ground.
Check young plants after planting. Harvest timing and outside inputs depend on the species, site and care; there is no guaranteed fifth-year result.

heading.text: Byala hi Ku Tsakama loku Tshembekaka
heading.backTranslation: Plant with Reliable Moisture

body.text: Hlawula nkarhi wo byala loko ku tsakama ka misava ni xiyimo xa moya lexi languteriweke swi seketela ku sungula.
body.backTranslation: Choose a planting time when the moisture of the soil and the expected climate support starting.

body.text: Mpfula yi nga pfuna, kambela root zone u tlhela u va ni pulani yo seketela ya ku cheleta mati. Papalata ku byala emisaveni leyi tatiweke hi mati.
body.backTranslation: Rain can help; check the root zone and also have a supporting plan for watering. Avoid planting in soil that is filled with water.

body.text: Kambela swimilana leswitsongo endzhaku ka ku byala. Nkarhi wa ntshovelo ni swilo leswi tisiwaka ku suka handle swi titshege hi xinxaka, ndhawu ni nhlayiso; a ku na xitshembiso xa vuyelo eka lembe ra vuntlhanu.
body.backTranslation: Check small plants after planting. Harvest time and things that are brought from outside depend on the kind, place and care; there is no promise of results in year five.

english.heading: Field Assignment
body: Draw the layers for your own proposed planting. Mark access, water and existing natural vegetation.
Record local frost, rain, soil and available care.
For each plant from the approved list, record its intended role and the local advice still needed before planting.

heading.text: Ntirho lowu u nyikiweke wa le nsimini
heading.backTranslation: The task given of the field

body.text: Dirowa swiyenge swa ku byala loku u ku kunguhateke. Komba ndlela yo fikelela, mati ni swimilana swa ntumbuluko leswi nga kona.
body.backTranslation: Draw the layers of planting that you have planned. Show the way of access, water and natural plants that are there.

body.text: Tsala xiqhwa, mpfula, misava ni nhlayiso lowu kumekaka laha kaya.
body.backTranslation: Write down the frost, rain, soil and maintenance found here/locally.

body.text: Eka swimilana swin’wana ni swin’wana leswi nga eka lisiti leyi pfumeriweke, tsala ntirho lowu swi kunguhatiweke ku wu endla ni ndzayo ya laha kaya leyi ha lavekaka u nga si byala.
body.backTranslation: For each plant that is on the approved list, write the task that it is planned to do and the local advice that is still needed before you plant.

english.heading: Field Action
body: Inspect a manageable area and choose one next step.
Protect exposed soil, check plant suitability, or prepare nursery plants.
Plant only when conditions and follow-up care are suitable. Return to the same spot to check survival, soil moisture and competition.

heading.text: Xiendlo xa le nsimini
heading.backTranslation: Field activity

body.text: Languta ndhawu leyi u nga kotaka ku yi hlayisa, kutani u hlawula goza rin’we leri landzelaka.
body.backTranslation: Look at the place that you can maintain, then choose one next step.

body.text: Sirhelela misava leyi nga funengetiwangiki, kambela ku fanela ka swimilana kumbe u lulamisa nursery plants.
body.backTranslation: Protect bare soil, check the suitability of plants or prepare nursery plants.

body.text: Byala ntsena loko swiyimo ni nhlayiso lowu landzelaka swi fanerile. Tlhelela endhawini yin’we ku ya kambela ku hanya, ku tsakama ka misava ni ku phikizana.
body.backTranslation: Plant only when the conditions and the maintenance that follows are right. Return to the same place to check survival, soil moisture and competition.
